# shellcheck shell=bash
# Shared PORT POLICY for every disposable-cluster harness (F-DG2-310, REQ-DLV-034). Sourced, never executed:
#   tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh, apps/web/e2e/support/with-stack.sh, e2e/support/qa-stack.sh,
#   e2e/clean-start/a18-clean-start.sh, deploy/scripts/clean-start-local.sh
#
# Why: the Linux ephemeral range (/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range, 32768-60999 by default) is where the kernel
# puts CLIENT sockets (psql, curl, the API's pool). A client socket that closes first stays in TIME_WAIT for ~60 s on
# its local port; a server that then binds that port fails with EADDRINUSE even with SO_REUSEADDR (the client socket
# did not set it). The old defaults (54331-54371) were inside that range, so a harness failed ~1 run in 6.
#
# Policy:
#   1. Defaults lie BELOW 32768 and are distinct per harness (PostgreSQL 24331/24340/24351/24361/24371; APIs
#      3000/3060/3100/3181). See docs/operations/clean-start.md "Harness port policy".
#   2. The requested port (default or from the environment) is the STARTING point. If the service fails to bind with
#      EADDRINUSE, it is restarted on another free port picked at random from MTH_PORT_POOL (default 25000-31999),
#      excluding the ephemeral range and any port with a socket in any state (/proc/net/tcp{,6}), at most
#      MTH_PORT_RETRIES (default 10) more times. Every retry is logged ("port-policy: ..." on stderr).
#   3. With the harness's <NAME>_STRICT_PORT=1 (or MTH_STRICT_PORT=1 for all), a bind conflict is not retried:
#      "BLOCKED: ..." and return 3.
#   4. Any failure that is NOT a bind conflict is never retried and never passes: mth_pg_start prints
#      "BLOCKED: disposable PostgreSQL did not start" and returns 3; mth_start_with_port_retry returns 1 and the
#      harness reports it (BLOCKED or FAIL, as before).
#   5. The caller exports its URLs from MTH_PORT / MTH_PG_PORT, the port actually in use.
#
# Functions
#   mth_pg_start <pgbin> <datadir> <logfile> <start-port> <strict-var> <pid-var> [extra postgres args...]
#       Starts postgres (as uid 1000 in a user namespace when run as root) on 127.0.0.1 only, no unix socket,
#       fsync=off. Sets MTH_PG_PORT and <pid-var> (the postmaster's PID, kept current during retries so the
#       caller's cleanup trap always sees it). Ready = the postmaster is alive and logged "ready to accept connections".
#   mth_start_with_port_retry <label> <start-port> <strict-var> <pid-var> <logfile> <timeout-s> <launch-fn> <ready-fn>
#       Generic form (used for the APIs). <launch-fn> <port> starts the service in the background, APPENDING its
#       output to <logfile>, and sets MTH_LAUNCHED_PID; <ready-fn> <port> returns 0 once it answers. Before each
#       launch the port is probed: a port on which something already ACCEPTS connections counts as in use (so a
#       foreign server can never be mistaken for ours). Sets MTH_PORT. Returns 0 ready, 3 BLOCKED (bind conflicts
#       exhausted / strict / invalid port / empty pool), 1 any other startup failure.
#       <pid-var> and <strict-var> are names of the CALLER's variables (set/read through printf -v / ${!name}); they
#       must not be one of this helper's local names (pid, port, strict, ...): the harnesses use PG_PID / API_PID.
#   mth_port_busy <port>   0 if any TCP socket uses the local port or something accepts connections on it.
#   mth_port_pick [tried ports...]   prints a random free pool port outside the ephemeral range.

MTH_PORT_POOL_DEFAULT="25000-31999"

mth_port_log() { echo "port-policy: $*" >&2; }

mth_port_ephemeral_range() {
  local r
  r="$(cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range 2>/dev/null || true)"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  set -- $r
  MTH_EPH_LO="${1:-32768}"

}
trap cleanup EXIT

[ -x "$PGBIN/initdb" ] || { echo "BLOCKED: PostgreSQL binaries not found (set PGBIN)"; exit 3; }
[ -f apps/api/dist/main.js ] && [ -f apps/web/dist/index.html ] || { echo "BLOCKED: run 'pnpm -r build' first"; exit 3; }

as_pg "$PGBIN/initdb" -D "$WORK/pg" -U postgres --auth=trust --encoding=UTF8 --locale=C >/dev/null
mth_pg_start "$PGBIN" "$WORK/pg" "$WORK/pg.log" "$PG_PORT" E2E_PG_STRICT_PORT PG_PID || exit 3
PG_PORT="$MTH_PG_PORT"
ADMIN_URL="postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:${PG_PORT}/postgres"
psql "$ADMIN_URL" -qAtc "select 1" >/dev/null || { echo "BLOCKED: disposable PostgreSQL did not start"; exit 3; }
psql "$ADMIN_URL" -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
  -c "CREATE ROLE mth_owner NOLOGIN" -c "CREATE ROLE mth_app NOLOGIN" \
  -c "CREATE DATABASE mth OWNER mth_owner ENCODING 'UTF8' LC_COLLATE 'C' LC_CTYPE 'C' TEMPLATE template0"
psql "$ADMIN_URL" -qAtc "select 'e2e database mth: server_encoding ' || pg_encoding_to_char(encoding) || ', lc_collate ' || datcollate || ', lc_ctype ' || datctype from pg_database where datname = 'mth'"

role_url() { node -e 'const u=new URL(process.argv[1]);u.pathname="/mth";u.searchParams.set("options","-c role="+process.argv[2]);console.log(u.toString())' "$ADMIN_URL" "$1"; }
export NODE_ENV=development AUTH_MODE=dev LOG_LEVEL=warn
# Evidence file revisions (P2) go to a private directory of this run; it is deleted with the cluster at teardown.
mkdir -p "$WORK/evidence"
export EVIDENCE_STORAGE_DRIVER=filesystem EVIDENCE_STORAGE_PATH="$WORK/evidence"
export DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$(role_url mth_owner)" DATABASE_URL="$(role_url mth_app)"
# The journeys sign in many times in a minute; production defaults are unchanged. E2E_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS=1 runs the
# API with the product's DEFAULT limits instead (both variables unset; session-end.spec.ts, F-DG2-480).
if [ "${E2E_DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITS:-}" = "1" ]; then
  unset AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE
  echo "rate limits: product defaults (AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE and RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE unset)"
else
  export AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=1000 RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=10000
fi

node packages/db/dist/cli.js migrate
node packages/db/dist/cli.js seed-dev
# PORT / APP_BASE_URL / E2E_BASE_URL follow the port of each attempt; after the start they hold the port in use.
launch_api() {
  export PORT="$1" APP_BASE_URL="http://localhost:$1" E2E_BASE_URL="http://localhost:$1"
  node apps/api/dist/main.js >>"$WORK/api.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
  MTH_LAUNCHED_PID=$!
}
api_ready() { curl -fsS "http://localhost:$1/readyz" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
RC=0
mth_start_with_port_retry "API" "$API_PORT" E2E_API_STRICT_PORT API_PID "$WORK/api.log" 30 launch_api api_ready || RC=$?
[ "$RC" = 3 ] && exit 3
[ "$RC" = 0 ] || { echo "API not ready"; cat "$WORK/api.log"; exit 4; }
API_PORT="$MTH_PORT"
echo "API: $E2E_BASE_URL (APP_BASE_URL=$APP_BASE_URL, PORT=$PORT)"
curl -fsS "$E2E_BASE_URL/readyz"
echo

set +e

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Holds a disposable PostgreSQL cluster for the DO-F load run: initdb, start, migrate, generate (default profile), then wait.
set -euo pipefail
cd /home/user/wt/dg6-do-f
export PATH=/opt/nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:$PATH
W="$TMPDIR/load"
PGBIN="$(ls -d /usr/lib/postgresql/*/bin | sort -V | tail -1)"
. tests/qa/support/pg-port.sh
as_pg() { if [ "$(id -u)" = "0" ]; then unshare --user --map-user=1000 --map-group=1000 "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }
mkdir -p "$W/pgroot"; chmod 777 "$W/pgroot"
as_pg "$PGBIN/initdb" -D "$W/pgroot/pg" -U postgres --auth=trust --encoding=UTF8 --locale=C >/dev/null
export MTH_PORT_POOL=25651-25669
mth_pg_start "$PGBIN" "$W/pgroot/pg" "$W/pg.log" 25650 QA_PG_STRICT_PORT PG_PID -c max_connections=200 || exit 3
echo "$MTH_PG_PORT" > "$W/pg.port"; echo "$PG_PID" > "$W/pg.pid"
trap 'kill -INT $PG_PID 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
ADMIN="postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$MTH_PG_PORT/postgres"
psql "$ADMIN" -qAtc "select version()"
psql "$ADMIN" -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "CREATE ROLE mth_owner NOLOGIN" -c "CREATE ROLE mth_app NOLOGIN" \
  -c "CREATE DATABASE mth OWNER mth_owner ENCODING 'UTF8' LC_COLLATE 'C' LC_CTYPE 'C' TEMPLATE template0"
OWN="postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$MTH_PG_PORT/mth?options=-c%20role%3Dmth_owner"
DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$OWN" DATABASE_URL="postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$MTH_PG_PORT/mth?options=-c%20role%3Dmth_app" node packages/db/dist/cli.js migrate
echo "== generate default start $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
s=$(date +%s.%N)
set +e; DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$OWN" node deploy/load/generate.mjs --profile default; rc=$?; set -e
echo "generate exit=$rc wall=$(echo "$(date +%s.%N) - $s" | bc) s end $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
touch "$W/generated.$rc"
while kill -0 "$PG_PID" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 5; done
EOF
chmod +x $TMPDIR/load/pg-hold.sh; echo $TMPDIR

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# T-DG6-DO-F, load run 1 (the first run; ADR-0058 §3-§6). The exact driver used for run-1, kept as evidence.
#
# Prerequisites (done by the caller, see the handback): a disposable PostgreSQL 16 cluster on 127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT with
# the database `mth` migrated and generated with `deploy/load/generate.mjs --profile default` (seed 20261027).
#
#   PG_PORT=25650 API_PORT=25680 RUN_DIR=docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/load/run-1 \
#     docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/load/run-1/driver.sh
#
# Per repetition: a freshly started API and worker (MTH_ENV=load, NODE_ENV=production, AUTH_MODE=oidc; product default
# rate limits), then `workload.mjs` (2 min warm-up, 10 min steady state), then both are stopped. Processes are stopped by
# their own PIDs only. The OIDC issuer below is never contacted: nobody logs in, the sessions are minted by
# deploy/load/sessions.mjs. No secret is involved: the database runs with trust authentication on loopback only.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
export PATH=/opt/nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:$PATH
: "${PG_PORT:?}" "${API_PORT:?}" "${RUN_DIR:?}"
REPS="${REPS:-3}" WARMUP_S="${WARMUP_S:-120}" STEADY_S="${STEADY_S:-600}"
WORK="$TMPDIR/load"
mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR" "$WORK/evidence" "$WORK/exports"
url() { echo "postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT/mth?options=-c%20role%3D$1"; }
export MTH_LOAD_DB_URL="postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT/mth"
export NODE_ENV=production MTH_ENV=load AUTH_MODE=oidc LOG_LEVEL=warn
export APP_BASE_URL="http://localhost:$API_PORT" PORT="$API_PORT"
export OIDC_ISSUER_URL="https://idp.example.invalid/realms/mth-load" OIDC_CLIENT_ID=mth-load OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=not-used-load-run
export DATABASE_URL="$(url mth_app)" DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$(url mth_owner)"
export EVIDENCE_STORAGE_DRIVER=filesystem EVIDENCE_STORAGE_PATH="$WORK/evidence"
unset RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE SEARCH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE EXPORT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE

API_PID="" WORKER_PID=""
stop() {
  for p in $API_PID $WORKER_PID; do kill -TERM "$p" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  for p in $API_PID $WORKER_PID; do for _ in $(seq 1 100); do kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done; done
  for p in $API_PID $WORKER_PID; do kill -KILL "$p" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  API_PID="" WORKER_PID=""
}
trap stop EXIT
start() {
  node apps/worker/dist/main.js >>"$WORK/worker-$1.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
  WORKER_PID=$!
  node apps/api/dist/main.js >>"$WORK/api-$1.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
  API_PID=$!
  for _ in $(seq 1 120); do curl -fsS "http://localhost:$API_PORT/readyz" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0; sleep 0.5; done
  echo "API not ready"; tail -50 "$WORK/api-$1.log"; return 1
}

echo "== driver start $(date -u +%FT%TZ); git HEAD $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
sha256sum deploy/load/generate.mjs deploy/load/sessions.mjs deploy/load/workload.mjs deploy/load/report.mjs

echo "== sessions $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
node deploy/load/sessions.mjs --duration-minutes 240 --out "$WORK/sessions.json"

echo "== search index: start the worker so it runs the requested search.reindex $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
start index
for _ in $(seq 1 360); do
  n=$(psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select count(*) from search_index_state where status = 'idle' and documents_count is not null")
  t=$(psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select count(*) from search_index_state")
  [ "$t" -gt 0 ] && [ "$n" = "$t" ] && break
  sleep 5
done
psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select record_type, status, documents_count, last_audit_seq from search_index_state order by 1"
echo "search index ready: $n of $t types $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
stop

echo "== infrastructure $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
node deploy/load/report.mjs capture-infra --out "$RUN_DIR/infrastructure.json" --pgdata "$WORK/pgroot/pg" \
  --api-processes 1 --api-pool 20 --worker-processes 1 --worker-pool 5

for rep in $(seq 1 "$REPS"); do
  echo "== repetition $rep: fresh API and worker $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  start "rep$rep"
  set +e
  node deploy/load/workload.mjs --sessions "$WORK/sessions.json" --base-url "http://127.0.0.1:$API_PORT" \
    --out "$RUN_DIR/rep-$rep" --warmup-s "$WARMUP_S" --steady-s "$STEADY_S" --repetition "$rep"
  rc=$?
  set -e
  echo "repetition $rep workload exit=$rc $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  stop
  grep -c '"level":50' "$WORK/api-rep$rep.log" | sed 's/^/api error-level log lines: /' || true
  [ "$rc" = 0 ] || exit "$rc"
done

echo "== report $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
node deploy/load/report.mjs report --run "$RUN_DIR" --title "DG6 load run 1 (first run, draft report; T-DG6-DO-F)"
echo "== driver end $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# T-DG6-DO-F, load run 1 (the first run; ADR-0058 §3-§6). The exact driver used for run-1, kept as evidence.
#
# Prerequisites (done by the caller, see the handback): a disposable PostgreSQL 16 cluster on 127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT with
# the database `mth` migrated and generated with `deploy/load/generate.mjs --profile default` (seed 20261027).
#
#   PG_PORT=25650 API_PORT=25680 RUN_DIR=docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-DO-F-evidence/load/run-1 \
#     docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-DO-F-evidence/load/run-1/driver.sh
#
# Per repetition: a freshly started API and worker (MTH_ENV=load, NODE_ENV=production, AUTH_MODE=oidc; product default
# rate limits), then `workload.mjs` (2 min warm-up, 10 min steady state), then both are stopped. Processes are stopped by
# their own PIDs only. The OIDC issuer below is never contacted: nobody logs in, the sessions are minted by
# deploy/load/sessions.mjs. No secret is involved: the database runs with trust authentication on loopback only.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
export PATH=/opt/nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:$PATH
: "${PG_PORT:?}" "${API_PORT:?}" "${RUN_DIR:?}"
REPS="${REPS:-3}" WARMUP_S="${WARMUP_S:-120}" STEADY_S="${STEADY_S:-600}"
WORK="$TMPDIR/load"
mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR" "$WORK/evidence"
url() { echo "postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT/mth?options=-c%20role%3D$1"; }
export MTH_LOAD_DB_URL="postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT/mth"
export NODE_ENV=production MTH_ENV=load AUTH_MODE=oidc LOG_LEVEL=warn
export APP_BASE_URL="http://localhost:$API_PORT" PORT="$API_PORT"
export OIDC_ISSUER_URL="https://idp.example.invalid/realms/mth-load" OIDC_CLIENT_ID=mth-load OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=not-used-load-run
DATABASE_URL="$(url mth_app)" DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$(url mth_owner)"
export DATABASE_URL DATABASE_OWNER_URL
export EVIDENCE_STORAGE_DRIVER=filesystem EVIDENCE_STORAGE_PATH="$WORK/evidence"
unset RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE SEARCH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE EXPORT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE

API_PID="" WORKER_PID=""
stop() {
  for p in $API_PID $WORKER_PID; do kill -TERM "$p" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  for p in $API_PID $WORKER_PID; do for _ in $(seq 1 100); do kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done; done
  for p in $API_PID $WORKER_PID; do kill -KILL "$p" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  API_PID="" WORKER_PID=""
}
trap stop EXIT
start() {
  node apps/worker/dist/main.js >>"$WORK/worker-$1.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
  WORKER_PID=$!
  node apps/api/dist/main.js >>"$WORK/api-$1.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
  API_PID=$!
  for _ in $(seq 1 120); do curl -fsS "http://localhost:$API_PORT/readyz" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0; sleep 0.5; done
  echo "API not ready"
  tail -50 "$WORK/api-$1.log"
  return 1
}

echo "== driver start $(date -u +%FT%TZ); git HEAD $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
sha256sum deploy/load/generate.mjs deploy/load/sessions.mjs deploy/load/workload.mjs deploy/load/report.mjs

echo "== sessions $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
node deploy/load/sessions.mjs --duration-minutes 240 --out "$WORK/sessions.json"

if [ "${SKIP_INDEX:-0}" != 1 ]; then
  echo "== search index: start the worker so it runs the requested search.reindex $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  start index
  n=0 t=0
  for _ in $(seq 1 360); do
    n=$(psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select count(*) from search_index_state where status = 'idle' and documents_count is not null")
    t=$(psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select count(*) from search_index_state")
    [ "$t" -gt 0 ] && [ "$n" = "$t" ] && break
    sleep 5
  done
  psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select record_type, status, documents_count, last_audit_seq from search_index_state order by 1"
  echo "search index ready: $n of $t types $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  stop
fi

echo "== infrastructure $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
node deploy/load/report.mjs capture-infra --out "$RUN_DIR/infrastructure.json" --pgdata "$WORK/pgroot/pg" \
  --api-processes 1 --api-pool 20 --worker-processes 1 --worker-pool 5

for rep in $(seq 1 "$REPS"); do
  echo "== repetition $rep: fresh API and worker $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  start "rep$rep"
  set +e
  node deploy/load/workload.mjs --sessions "$WORK/sessions.json" --base-url "http://127.0.0.1:$API_PORT" \
    --out "$RUN_DIR/rep-$rep" --warmup-s "$WARMUP_S" --steady-s "$STEADY_S" --repetition "$rep"
  rc=$?
  set -e
  echo "repetition $rep workload exit=$rc $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  stop
  echo "api error-level log lines: $(grep -c '"level":50' "$WORK/api-rep$rep.log" || true)"
  [ "$rc" = 0 ] || exit "$rc"
done

echo "== report $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
node deploy/load/report.mjs report --run "$RUN_DIR" --title "DG6 load run 1 (first run, draft report; T-DG6-DO-F)"
echo "== driver end $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Restarts the disposable load cluster on its existing data directory and holds it while it accepts connections.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Starts the disposable load cluster on its existing data directory and runs queued command files ($W/q/NNN.sh) inside
# this one process tree (separate sandboxed commands do not share a network namespace). Output: NNN.log, NNN.rc.
set -uo pipefail

W="$TMPDIR/load"; mkdir -p "$W/q"

echo "$MTH_PG_PORT" > "$W/pg.port"
echo "postgres on $MTH_PG_PORT $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
trap 'kill -INT "$PG_PID" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
while [ ! -f "$W/q/stop" ]; do
  for f in "$W"/q/*.sh; do
    [ -e "$f" ] || continue
    [ -e "${f%.sh}.rc" ] && continue
    echo "run $f $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
    PG_PORT="$MTH_PG_PORT" bash "$f" >"${f%.sh}.log" 2>&1
    echo $? > "${f%.sh}.rc"
    echo "done $f rc=$(cat "${f%.sh}.rc") $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  done
  sleep 2
done
EOF

input.command:
cd /home/user/wt/dg6-do-f; python3 - <<'EOF'
p="docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-DO-F-evidence/load/run-1/driver.sh"
s=open(p).read()
a='''    n=$(psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select count(*) from search_index_state where status = 'idle' and documents_count is not null")
    t=$(psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select count(*) from search_index_state")
    [ "$t" -gt 0 ] && [ "$n" = "$t" ] && break'''
b='''    # Ready = the generator's requested search.reindex job has completed and no record type is still reindexing.
    n=$(psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select count(*) from pgboss.job where name = 'search.reindex' and state = 'completed'")
    t=$(psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select count(*) from search_index_state where status <> 'idle'")
    [ "$n" -ge 1 ] && [ "$t" = 0 ] && break'''
assert a in s; s=s.replace(a,b)
s=s.replace('''  psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select record_type, status, documents_count, last_audit_seq from search_index_state order by 1"
  echo "search index ready: $n of $t types $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"''','''  psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select record_type, status, documents_count, last_audit_seq from search_index_state order by 1" \\
    -c "select name, state, count(*) from pgboss.job where name like 'search.%' group by 1, 2 order by 1, 2" \\
    -c "select record_type, count(*) from search_document group by 1 order by 1"
  echo "search index: reindex completed jobs $n, types not idle $t $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"''')
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF

input.command:
cat > $TMPDIR/load/q/010.sh <<'EOF'
# T-DG6-DO-F: the EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) diagnostic pass after run-1 (unmeasured; auto_explain, then reset).
set -uo pipefail
cd /home/user/wt/dg6-do-f
export PATH=/opt/nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:$PATH
E=docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-DO-F-evidence/load/run-1
W=$TMPDIR/load; API_PORT=25682
[ "$(cat $W/q/009.rc)" = 0 ] || { echo "run-1 driver did not succeed; no diagnostic pass"; exit 1; }
echo "== apply the --only option to workload.mjs (after the measured run) $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
python3 $W/add-only.py deploy/load/workload.mjs && sha256sum deploy/load/workload.mjs
url() { echo "postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT/mth?options=-c%20role%3D$1"; }
D="postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT/mth"
export MTH_LOAD_DB_URL="$D" NODE_ENV=production MTH_ENV=load AUTH_MODE=oidc LOG_LEVEL=warn
export APP_BASE_URL="http://localhost:$API_PORT" PORT="$API_PORT"
export OIDC_ISSUER_URL="https://idp.example.invalid/realms/mth-load" OIDC_CLIENT_ID=mth-load OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=not-used-load-run
export DATABASE_URL="$(url mth_app)" EVIDENCE_STORAGE_DRIVER=filesystem EVIDENCE_STORAGE_PATH="$W/evidence"
OPS=$(node -e '
const s=require(process.argv[1]);const t={read:2000,update:2000,search:2000,dashboard:4000,export:2000};
console.log(s.perOperation.filter(o=>Math.max(...o.perRep.map(r=>r.p95??0))>t[o.cls]*1000).map(o=>o.operation).join(" "))' "$PWD/$E/summary.json")
echo "operations whose highest p95 misses its class target: ${OPS:-none}"
[ -n "$OPS" ] || exit 0
psql "$D" -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "ALTER DATABASE mth SET session_preload_libraries = 'auto_explain'" \
  -c "ALTER DATABASE mth SET auto_explain.log_min_duration = '100ms'" -c "ALTER DATABASE mth SET auto_explain.log_analyze = on" \
  -c "ALTER DATABASE mth SET auto_explain.log_buffers = on" -c "ALTER DATABASE mth SET auto_explain.log_nested_statements = on" \
  -c "ALTER DATABASE mth SET auto_explain.log_timing = on"
mkdir -p "$E/explain"
node apps/worker/dist/main.js >>"$W/worker-diag.log" 2>&1 </dev/null & WK=$!
node apps/api/dist/main.js >>"$W/api-diag2.log" 2>&1 </dev/null & AP=$!
for _ in $(seq 1 120); do curl -fsS "http://localhost:$API_PORT/readyz" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 0.5; done
for op in $OPS; do
  # 5 users: about the measured request rate of one operation, inside the export class's 10/min/user budget.
  echo "== diagnostic pass $op $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  psql "$D" -qc "DO \$\$ BEGIN RAISE LOG 'mth-diag start $op'; END \$\$"
  node deploy/load/workload.mjs --sessions "$W/sessions.json" --base-url "http://127.0.0.1:$API_PORT" --out "$W/diag-$op" \
    --warmup-s 0 --steady-s 60 --repetition 200 --users 5 --only "$op"
  psql "$D" -qc "DO \$\$ BEGIN RAISE LOG 'mth-diag end $op'; END \$\$"
  sleep 1
  awk -v s="mth-diag start $op" -v e="mth-diag end $op" 'index($0,s){on=1} on{print} index($0,e){on=0}' "$W/pg.log" > "$E/explain/$op.auto-explain.log"
  echo "$op: $(grep -c 'duration: .* ms  plan:' "$E/explain/$op.auto-explain.log") plan(s) logged; $(wc -c < "$E/explain/$op.auto-explain.log") bytes"
  cp "$W/diag-$op/run.json" "$E/explain/$op.diagnostic-run.json"
done
kill $AP $WK; wait $AP $WK 2>/dev/null
psql "$D" -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "ALTER DATABASE mth RESET ALL"
psql "$D" -qAtc "select coalesce(string_agg(array_to_string(setconfig, ','), ';'), 'none') from pg_db_role_setting s join pg_database d on d.oid = s.setdatabase where d.datname = 'mth'"
echo "== diagnostic end $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
EOF
echo queued; tail -3 $TMPDIR/load/q/009.log

Decisions:**
**ARCH-04 §5:** (1) bulk updates stay all-or-nothing as at DG5; the DG5 response that lists only the stale records meets 'a conflict for that record only' (no reopen). (2) The 'full load dataset' export is read as ADR-0058 §7 states: the largest transformation's full selection (xlsx, csv) plus 50 concurrent exports, one per transformation; no cross-transformation export. (3) The search index jobs may read sensitive records' indexed columns only (titles, codes, descriptions; no value column) under an explicit ADR-0053 exception, with readers filtered at query time. (4) Server-side sort and text filters on the 11 list operations ADR-0057 §5 names; no other list in DG6. (5) Draft recovery covers the form-record editors. (6) **Comparison values: the `audit.read`-only variant** (the DG5 rule in `forms/history.ts` is kept; editors see field names only, no widening). (7) The DG2 register-kit list description ('newest change first') is corrected to the code's order (`id` ascending) by BE-F2 as a contract-text fix; no behaviour change. (8) Splits accepted: BE-P/P2, BE-Q/Q2, FE-D/D2. (9) `MTH_ENV=load` with its two start-up refusals is confirmed (D-195 Q9).
**BE-B2 §6:** the optional `includesRestrictedRecords` property is added to `BenefitTotals`, `TransformationDashboard`, `WorkstreamDashboard`, `FinanceDashboard`, `DashboardDrilldown` and their zod mirrors (additive, D-196 item 4) by BE-F2; the export refusal gets its own code `export.includes_restricted_records` (403, English text as proposed; Arabic provisional).
**BE-F §5 (defects found by the integrity sweep, repaired during the build):** `archiveEvidence` and `removeEvidenceLink` accept evidence that supports an approved gate decision (expected 409). **T-DG6-BE-F2** adds the 'finalized evidence' rule (409 `evidence.finalized`, 'This evidence supports an approved gate decision and cannot be archived or unlinked.') and removes the two `it.fails` marks. The 38 `list*` operations without `nextCursor`: ARCH-05 amends ADR-0007/0052 to exempt bounded collections **by name, each with its bound stated**, and any list it cannot bound gets pagination in a later task.
**DO-A §0 (security):** the dependency audit runs live through the proxy and finds 20 High advisories in shipped packages (fastify 5.6.1, @fastify/static 8.2.0, kysely 0.28.7, zod 4.1.12, react-router 7.9.0, image-size 1.2.1 via pptxgenjs). **Decision: upgrade, not a risk acceptance.** **T-DG6-DO-A2** (devops) upgrades them (fastify ≥ 5.12.2, @fastify/static ≥ 10.1.1, kysely ≥ 0.28.17, zod ≥ 4.6.6, react-router ≥ 7.18.0, image-size ≥ 2.0.3 by override, verified against pptxgenjs' exports), plus the dev toolchain (vitest ≥ 3.2.6, tinypool, vite), adds `@aws-sdk/client-s3@3.1156.0` and `nodemailer@10.2.1` (D-197), refreshes the SBOM and the advisory snapshot, and runs every test including the full e2e. The orchestrator installs `deploy/ci/ci.yml` as `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and confirms the `vitest.config.ts` include line; ARCH-05 corrects ADR-0052 §6's 'BLOCKED in this sandbox' wording.
**W5:** T-DG6-ARCH-05 (slice D, the assistant, plus the ADR amendments above), T-DG6-BE-C (deep links, inbox redaction, evidence after ownership transfer), T-DG6-BE-F2, T-DG6-DO-A2. BE-J moves to W6. | W4 handbacks. | — | 11:| D-197 | 2026-10-26 | delivery-orchestrator | **W2 is integrated: T-DG6-ARCH-02 (slices J + C: ADR-0053 operations and service identities, ADR-0054 identity, storage and notification channels; their migrations from `0101`, contract and work-split sections) and T-DG6-BE-A (P6 module registry, stubs and wiring points; merge `32dc271`). Decisions on the raised points:**
1. **Keycloak (D-195 Q5).** The Docker Hub publication could not be verified as the vendor's own from official documentation (the D-195 condition), but quay.io is now reachable. DO-B resolves and pins `quay.io/keycloak/keycloak` by digest with `pin-images.mjs` (moving 26.4 to the current 26.x the ADR names). The Keycloak e2e still needs a container runtime, which this sandbox lacks, so it remains a disclosed residual (D-049) and the cross-realm rejection is proven with the local fake OP.
2. **Dependencies (D-195 Q7, ADR-0054): Option A.** The registry is reachable (`npm view` on 2026-10-26): `@aws-sdk/client-s3@3.1156.0` (Apache-2.0) and `nodemailer@10.2.1` (MIT-0, 0 dependencies; support window [UNVERIFIED], disclosed). The orchestrator adds them, exact-pinned, in the package each ADR names before BE-H and BE-I start; DO-A refreshes the SBOM and licence inventory.
3. **Connector exceptions and KPI freshness (ADR-0053 §2):** no. An active connector exception does not force a KPI to `stale`; the DG4 freshness rule stays unchanged (no reopen). The A17/A22 fixtures use actuals older than `staleAfterDays`.
4. **Task splits accepted:** BE-J/J2/J3, BE-K/K2, BE-H/H2, BE-I/I2 (+5 runs).
5. **The audit routes' access (BE-A §4.1):** the injected port (`AuditRouteAccess`, the GateFactsProvider pattern) is accepted, because `audit → access` is a module cycle; ADR-0052 §8's file stays `audit/routes.ts`, and BE-E fills the port.
**W3:** T-DG6-ARCH-03 (slices B + A) in the main checkout; T-DG6-BE-B (§E/F.2), T-DG6-BE-E (§E/F.7) and T-DG6-FE-A (shell, i18n, API client) in worktrees. | ARCH-02 and BE-A handbacks. | — | 12:| D-196 | 2026-10-26 | delivery-orchestrator | **T-DG6-ARCH-01 (slices E + F) is integrated: ADR-0051 (authorization boundary) and ADR-0052 (request and input hardening), migrations `0098`–`0100`, 13 operations (contract `1.5.0-p6`, 859 operations), `p6-work-split.md` §2 and §E/F. No DG1–DG5 behaviour changes (every new column nullable; probe G04). The architect's §5 questions are decided:**
1. **REQ-S13-013, 403 vs 404 (ADR-0051 §4): Option A.** A caller without `transformation.read` keeps the DG2-approved 404 (non-disclosure); an in-scope caller without admission to the evidence's parent record (or to a sensitive item) gets 403 `evidence.parent_forbidden`. This matches the acceptance text 'a user without access to the parent gets 403'; no DG2 reopen.
2. **Migration ids:** ARCH ranges are advisory. An implementer's migration takes the next id above the highest shipped file at merge time (the orchestrator renumbers at merge if needed), and every skipped id is recorded as retired (the F-DG5-100 runner rule; p5-work-split rule 16).
3. **Task splits accepted:** BE-B2 after BE-B (W3), BE-C2 after BE-C (W4), BE-E2 after BE-E and BE-D (W5); the waves grow by three runs.
4. **BE-B2's contract additions** (optional `includesRestrictedRecords` on DG4/DG5 aggregate schemas) are additive under D-195 Q3; accepted, listed in its handback.
5. **`inbox.restricted` texts** as in ADR-0051 §3; the Arabic stays labelled provisional.
6. **FE-B ownership extension accepted:** `pages/admin/security/**`, `components/sensitivity/**`, `components/evidence-preview/**`, each mounted by one named line in existing detail pages.
**Then W2:** T-DG6-ARCH-02 (slices J + C) in the main checkout, with T-DG6-BE-A (P6 registry, stubs and wiring points) in its own worktree. | `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-ARCH-01-solution-architect.md`. | — | 13:| D-195 | 2026-10-26 | delivery-orchestrator (Q3, Q5 and the adoption of the remaining recommendations decided by the user) | **The P6 plan (`docs/architecture/p6-plan.md`, T-DG6-ARCH-00) is adopted.** 48 DG6 requirements in slices A–L (Met 0, Partly 35, New 13); 6 architecture tasks (ADR-0051…0062, migrations from 0098, advisory locks from 730300), 37 implementer runs, 5 QA runs and the analyst run, in 14 waves of at most 4 concurrent runs.
**Open questions, decided:**
- **Q3 (user): sensitive records.** Sensitivity applies to Benefit, BusinessCase and Evidence first; only TO and the access admin grant; a user without the grant sees aggregates that include the value, labelled 'includes restricted records' (en/ar), never the record or its individual value. Totals stay identical for every user (no DG4 reopen).
- **Q5 (user): Keycloak.** ARCH-02 verifies from official documentation that Docker Hub `keycloak/keycloak` is the vendor's own publication; if verified, it is pinned by digest and the e2e logs in through the test realm; if not, the e2e stays BLOCKED as a disclosed residual (D-049), and the cross-realm rejection is proven with the local fake OP.
- **Q1, Q2, Q4, Q6–Q14 (user: adopt the architect's recommendations):** Q1 Imports under 'Strategy and KPIs' with an entry in Administration > Integrations, no fifteenth area; Q2 evidence links are API paths with a single-use token (default 5 minutes, configurable), re-authorized on use, bytes proxied in both storage modes, no object-store URL reaches the client; Q4 upload allow-list PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, CSV, TXT, PNG, JPEG, GIF by magic bytes plus extension, IT-configurable, SVG download-only, earlier files untouched; Q6 an in-process S3-protocol fake for the contract suite, a licence-reviewed store documented for IT, the live store a residual; Q7 a vetted SMTP library only if the registry is provisioned, a local fake SMTP for the contract test, live mail a residual, enterprise messaging port only; Q8 A21 on `compose.no-egress.yaml` plus a test-mode connection log of every outbound attempt (named a connection log, not a packet capture; a full capture is a DG7/A18 check); Q9 the load run on the sandbox host (stated hardware and settings), sessions minted in a `MTH_ENV=load` database, a Node harness without a new dependency, each p95 miss a Medium, non-mandatory finding; Q10 the CI dependency-audit job plus an offline SBOM check against a dated committed advisory snapshot, the live audit BLOCKED in the sandbox; Q11 XLSX formula cells refused as row errors, formula-like CSV text imported as text; Q12 'creates' means the API mutation that produces the entity; Q13 job identities enforced in the application through `ReadScope` with a test per job, no PostgreSQL RLS; Q14 downstream writes only as connector-defined actions on the test adapter, no live downstream write claimed.
- **Reopen candidates (p6-plan §3, R7):** sensitive totals (row 2) are additive under Q3; the upload allow-list (row 3) applies to new uploads only under Q4; inbox title redaction (row 6) and branding contrast refusal (row 18) are accepted as stated in the plan, each with its exact en/ar text in its ADR; any other change to approved behaviour is brought to the user first.
**Then:** W1 is T-DG6-ARCH-01 (slices E + F), alone. | `docs/architecture/p6-plan.md`; `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-ARCH-00-solution-architect.md`. | — |

input.content:
- **Status: draft report of the FIRST run (T-DG6-DO-F, §H/G.8).** It is not the final load report: BE-S (fixes named here) and DO-G (the final run on the frozen tree) follow. The workload, dataset and infrastructure were not changed after the run to turn a miss into a pass (ADR-0058 §1, p6-plan R4).
- **The host was heavily oversubscribed.** The 1-minute load average was 15.5–21.0 on 4 logical CPUs during every repetition (table in §6). Other agents' builds and test suites ran on the same host throughout; their CPU use is inside these figures, together with the harness's own client-side CPU. The figures are therefore pessimistic for this code on this hardware, and they are not comparable with any production sizing.
- **Generator patch (disclosed).** `deploy/load/generate.mjs` at sha256 `7470ea74…` derives ids as `md5(key)::uuid`, which have no RFC 9562 version or variant bits. The API's UUID validation refuses them (`400 validation.invalid_format "Invalid UUID"`; `smoke-diagnosis-invalid-uuid.txt`), so about 88 % of initiatives and most transformations could not be addressed through the API. The dataset of this run was generated by a copy of the generator with the minimal patch `generate-rfc-uuid.patch` (sha256 of the patched copy `6b2a9007…`): the same md5 with the version-3 and variant bits set. The tree file was **not** changed (DO-E's file); adopting the patch is for the orchestrator. Generation: exit 0, 384.9 s, marker counts = planned counts, 100,000 audit events, 0 non-RFC ids in `initiative`, `transformation` and `audit_event`, 154 MB.
- **Smoke requests before the run.** Two short harness smokes (repetitions 91 and 92; about 1,300 requests, not measured, results discarded) and the worker's indexing ran on the generated database before `capture-infra`, so the database held 100,894 audit events (not 100,000) when run-1 started; each repetition adds its own update events. Saved views `LOAD view u{n} r91`/`r92` and their drafts and exports from the smokes remain in the database.
- **Not measured: `getWorkstreamDashboard`.** The `default` profile of the generator writes no `workstream` row (0 rows), so no user has a workstream to read. The operation is in ADR-0058 §3's mix but has no sample; it is reported as not measured, never as 0 or a pass. The other four dashboards are measured. A generator change (workstreams) is a DO-E/orchestrator decision.
- **Class draw.** Users whose roles hold no operation of a class leave that class out of their own draw: 5 AUD users (no update, no export), 50 users without a saved view or draft target (AUD has no `saved_view.manage`; `createFormDraft` T05 refused 403 for 50 users) and 50 users with an initiative partition (holders of `initiative.edit`). The achieved shares are within 1 point of the ADR shares (§5 table).
- **Search index.** The generator's requested `search.reindex` completed before the run (driver output); the index then held 400 benefits, 500 decisions, 1,000 deliverables, 500 dependencies, 1,000 evidence notes, 1,000 initiatives, 500 KPI definitions, 1,500 RAID entries and 50 transformations. The scheduled `search.index_feed` (every minute) ran during the repetitions, as in production.
- **Export start miss (the only class miss).** `createExport` of a live selection builds its report snapshot inside the request (ADR-0046), so its latency includes the snapshot assembly. The EXPLAIN diagnostic pass (`explain/`, unmeasured, run after the three repetitions with `auto_explain` `log_analyze`, `log_buffers`, `log_nested_statements`, then reset) found **no single statement over 100 ms** with 5 concurrent exporters (`createExport.auto-explain-over-100ms.log` holds only the pass markers). With every statement logged (1 user, 7 requests: 144–2,642 ms each), the cost is in statement volume: `report_snapshot_source` is inserted row by row (759 inserts for 7 exports, 591 ms in total), the scoped-assignment permission query runs about 41 times per request (290 calls), the deferred `p2_audit_required` check (the T-DG6-DO-E candidate: `record_type = TG_TABLE_NAME`, type `name`) costs up to 64.5 ms per call, and the roadmap assembler reads initiatives and dependencies once per row (265 calls each). Digest with the full plans: `explain/createExport.explain-digest-all-statements.md`; full log: `explain/createExport.auto-explain.all-statements.log.gz`.
- **Disclosed harness errors, superseded.** The first diagnostic pass ran its API on port 25682 while the minted sessions record `APP_BASE_URL` on 25681, so all 146 requests got `403 csrf` (`explain/invalid-first-diagnostic-pass-csrf-403.txt`); it was repeated on 25681. The first smoke (on the unpatched dataset) also lacked `organizationId` on two dashboards and the browser `Origin` header on writes; both were fixed in the harness before run-1. None of these affected the three measured repetitions, which had 0 errors.

- **Status: draft report of the FIRST run (T-DG6-DO-F, §H/G.8).** It is not the final load report: BE-S (fixes named here) and DO-G (the final run on the frozen tree) follow. The workload, dataset and infrastructure were not changed after the run to turn a miss into a pass (ADR-0058 §1, p6-plan R4).
- **The host was heavily oversubscribed.** The 1-minute load average was 15.5–21.0 on 4 logical CPUs during every repetition (table in §6). Other agents' builds and test suites ran on the same host throughout; their CPU use is inside these figures, together with the harness's own client-side CPU. The figures are therefore pessimistic for this code on this hardware, and they are not comparable with any production sizing.
- **Generator patch (disclosed).** `deploy/load/generate.mjs` at sha256 `7470ea74…` derives ids as `md5(key)::uuid`, which have no RFC 9562 version or variant bits. The API's UUID validation refuses them (`400 validation.invalid_format "Invalid UUID"`; `smoke-diagnosis-invalid-uuid.txt`), so about 88 % of initiatives and most transformations could not be addressed through the API. The dataset of this run was generated by a copy of the generator with the minimal patch `generate-rfc-uuid.patch` (sha256 of the patched copy `6b2a9007…`): the same md5 with the version-3 and variant bits set. The tree file was **not** changed (DO-E's file); adopting the patch is for the orchestrator. Generation: exit 0, 384.9 s, marker counts = planned counts, 100,000 audit events, 0 non-RFC ids in `initiative`, `transformation` and `audit_event`, 154 MB.
- **Smoke requests before the run.** Two short harness smokes (repetitions 91 and 92; about 1,300 requests, not measured, results discarded) and the worker's indexing ran on the generated database before `capture-infra`, so the database held 100,894 audit events (not 100,000) when run-1 started; each repetition adds its own update events. Saved views `LOAD view u{n} r91`/`r92` and their drafts and exports from the smokes remain in the database.
- **Not measured: `getWorkstreamDashboard`.** The `default` profile of the generator writes no `workstream` row (0 rows), so no user has a workstream to read. The operation is in ADR-0058 §3's mix but has no sample; it is reported as not measured, never as 0 or a pass. The other four dashboards are measured. A generator change (workstreams) is a DO-E/orchestrator decision.
- **Class draw.** Users whose roles hold no operation of a class leave that class out of their own draw: 5 AUD users (no update, no export), 50 users without a saved view or draft target (AUD has no `saved_view.manage`; `createFormDraft` T05 refused 403 for 50 users) and 50 users with an initiative partition (holders of `initiative.edit`). The achieved shares are within 1 point of the ADR shares (§5 table).
- **Search index.** The generator's requested `search.reindex` completed before the run (driver output); the index then held 400 benefits, 500 decisions, 1,000 deliverables, 500 dependencies, 1,000 evidence notes, 1,000 initiatives, 500 KPI definitions, 1,500 RAID entries and 50 transformations. The scheduled `search.index_feed` (every minute) ran during the repetitions, as in production.
- **Export start miss (the only class miss).** `createExport` of a live selection builds its report snapshot inside the request (ADR-0046), so its latency includes the snapshot assembly. The EXPLAIN diagnostic pass (`explain/`, unmeasured, run after the three repetitions with `auto_explain` `log_analyze`, `log_buffers`, `log_nested_statements`, then reset) found **no single statement over 100 ms** with 5 concurrent exporters (`createExport.auto-explain-over-100ms.log` holds only the pass markers). With every statement logged (1 user, 7 requests: 144–2,642 ms each), the cost is in statement volume: `report_snapshot_source` is inserted row by row (759 inserts for 7 exports, 591 ms in total), the scoped-assignment permission query runs about 41 times per request (290 calls), the deferred `p2_audit_required` check (the T-DG6-DO-E candidate: `record_type = TG_TABLE_NAME`, type `name`) costs up to 64.5 ms per call, and the roadmap assembler reads initiatives and dependencies once per row (265 calls each). Digest with the full plans: `explain/createExport.explain-digest-all-statements.md`; full log: `explain/createExport.auto-explain.all-statements.log.gz`.
- **Disclosed harness errors, superseded.** The first diagnostic pass ran its API on port 25682 while the minted sessions record `APP_BASE_URL` on 25681, so all 146 requests got `403 csrf` (`explain/invalid-first-diagnostic-pass-csrf-403.txt`); it was repeated on 25681. The first smoke (on the unpatched dataset) also lacked `organizationId` on two dashboards and the browser `Origin` header on writes; both were fixed in the harness before run-1. None of these affected the three measured repetitions, which had 0 errors.

input.content:
# Handback: T-DG6-DO-F, the workload harness and the first load run (devops-engineer)

- **Stage:** DG6 (P6 "Integration and system hardening"), BUILDING. This handback decides nothing about the DG6 engineering gate. Product gates G1–G6 are untouched, and nothing here grants a business, Finance or IT approval. The load dataset and its users are synthetic.
- **Assignment:** `docs/delivery/assignments/DG6/T-DG6-DO-F.md` (sha256 `ecd52273…bc2f3ec`, verified). Scope: `docs/architecture/p6-work-split.md` §H/G.8, ADR-0058 §1, §3, §5, §6, §10.
- **Invocation:** `DG6-T-DG6-DO-F-devops-engineer-20261030T074016Z-2eec07bc`, session `2eec07bc-da74-4fed-bb0d-f0d176b7afb4`.
- **Working tree:** `/home/user/wt/dg6-do-f`, branch `dg6/do-f`, base `HEAD` `9ca454f20cc830f85ecd7d70d9e873370c98c60c`. The changes are **uncommitted**.
- **Time:** started `2026-10-30T07:40:36Z`; finished at `__END__` (see §8).
- **Evidence:** `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-DO-F-evidence/`. The run is in `load/run-1/` (see §6, item 1).

## 0. Preceding gate

`node tools/gates/validate.mjs --historical --stage DG5` → **exit 0**, `PASS gate DG5 (historical)`, 2 m 58.7 s (`validate-dg5-historical.txt`).

## 1. Changed files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `deploy/load/workload.mjs` (new) | ADR-0058 §3, §6 harness. 100 concurrent virtual users, each with its own minted session, and the class mix by share. Deterministic integer mulberry32 draws per (seed, repetition, user) and think time of 1000–3000 ms. Integer-microsecond samples (`performance.now()`, start of `fetch` to end of body). Warm-up is excluded and the load average is sampled every 5 s. The update targets are partitioned (each initiative goes to exactly one editor). It refuses a database without the load marker. `--only` is for diagnostic passes only. |
| `deploy/load/report.mjs` (new) | `capture-infra`: the §5 infrastructure statement, measured at the run (CPU, memory, kernel, Node, PostgreSQL version and non-default settings, the process and pool sizes, `df`, the marker and counts, the search index state). `report`: nearest-rank p50/p95/p99, max, count, errors and 409s per class per repetition. The class result is the highest p95 of the repetitions. It also gives per-operation figures, achieved shares, request templates and load average. Operations without samples are listed as "not measured". Run notes are embedded. |
| `deploy/load/harness.node-test.mjs` (new) | 7 self-tests with Node's built-in runner: nearest-rank, null (not 0) when unmeasured, integer µs, the shares of the draw, think-time determinism and range, the partition (each initiative goes to exactly one editor), and search terms. |
| `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG6/T-DG6-DO-F-*` | This handback, the run-1 evidence (driver, samples, report, EXPLAIN), the check logs and the generator patch. |

No migration, no new dependency, no OpenAPI, zod or schema change, and no operation routed.

## 2. Behaviour delivered

**REQ-S20-029.** Acceptance: "A22;A13: the load report states the dataset, infrastructure and workload, and gives actual p95 figures for reads/updates and dashboards, with any miss against 2 s/4 s listed as a finding".

DO-F's part is delivered: the harness, the report generator, and the first run with its draft report (`load/run-1/report.md`). That report states:

- the dataset: the marker row and the counts at capture;
- the infrastructure, as measured;
- the workload: templates, shares, think time, window and repetitions;
- actual p50/p95/p99/max per class for each of 3 repetitions;
- the miss, listed as a finding candidate.

**The row is not complete:** BE-S (fixes) and DO-G (the final run on the frozen tree) follow (§H/G.13).

Run-1 results. Steady state is 10 min per repetition after a 2 min warm-up, on a freshly started API and worker each time. 100 users, seed 20261027, nearest-rank, figures in ms:

| Class (target) | rep-1 p95 | rep-2 p95 | rep-3 p95 | Highest p95 | Result | Requests (3 reps) | Errors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary read (2 s) | 745.8 | 658.2 | 681.2 | 745.8 | within | 40,010 | 0 |
| Ordinary update (2 s) | 1,007.4 | 918.0 | 980.3 | 1,007.4 | within | 11,126 | 0 (0 × 409) |
| Search (2 s) | 748.2 | 634.1 | 707.2 | 748.2 | within | 6,474 | 0 |
| Key dashboard (4 s) | 1,185.3 | 1,097.6 | 1,191.2 | 1,191.2 | within | 20,021 | 0 |
| Export start (2 s) | 2,688.1 | 2,257.2 | 2,453.3 | **2,688.1** | **MISS** | 1,483 | 0 |
| Ordinary read incl. search (2 s) | 745.9 | 655.8 | 687.4 | 745.9 | within | 46,484 | 0 |

- Steady-state requests per repetition: 26,393, 26,424 and 26,297. Warm-up requests (excluded): 4,872, 5,268 and 4,792. Samples per file: 31,265, 31,692 and 31,089 rows.
- **Finding candidate (Medium, non-mandatory; ADR-0058 §1, D-195 Q9): Export start p95 2,688.1 ms > 2 s.** The orchestrator allocates the id.
  - Cause, from the EXPLAIN pass: `createExport` of a live selection assembles the report snapshot inside the request. No single statement exceeded 100 ms (5 concurrent exporters). The cost is volume:
    - `report_snapshot_source` is inserted row by row (759 inserts for 7 exports);
    - the scoped-assignment permission query runs about 41× per request;
    - the deferred `p2_audit_required` check costs up to 64.5 ms per call (DO-E's `TG_TABLE_NAME` candidate);
    - initiatives and dependencies are read once per row (265× each).
  - Digest with plans: `load/run-1/explain/createExport.explain-digest-all-statements.md`.
  - These are BE-S's inputs (§H/G.9). I made no fix.
- **Not measured:** `getWorkstreamDashboard`. The `default` dataset has no `workstream` row (§5, item 3).
- **Honesty.** The host was oversubscribed during the whole run: 1-minute load average 15.5–21.0 on 4 CPUs, mostly other agents' work. These are sandbox engineering measurements, not Mobily production capacity. One host is not high availability, and the targets are provisional (REQ-S20-029 notes). All of this is stated in the report.

**REQ-S20-030** is not DO-F's: the export proof belongs to BE-S, and the final run to DO-G.

## 3. Checks actually run

Environment for every check:

- Host: 4 vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.80GHz, 16 GB RAM, no swap, kernel 6.18.44-fc-v185, Node 24.21.0, pnpm 10.33.0.
- Load cluster: a disposable PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster on 127.0.0.1:25650 (`fsync=off`, `max_connections=200`, `shared_buffers` 128 MB).
- Integration cluster: on ports 25670–25699.
- Offline. Other agents shared the host.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# T-DG6-DO-F, load run 1 (the first run; ADR-0058 §3-§6). The exact driver used for run-1, kept as evidence.
#
# Prerequisites (done by the caller, see the handback): a disposable PostgreSQL 16 cluster on 127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT with
# the database `mth` migrated and generated with `deploy/load/generate.mjs --profile default` (seed 20261027).
#
#   PG_PORT=25650 API_PORT=25680 RUN_DIR=docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/load/run-1 \
#     docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/load/run-1/driver.sh
#
# Per repetition: a freshly started API and worker (MTH_ENV=load, NODE_ENV=production, AUTH_MODE=oidc; product default
# rate limits), then `workload.mjs` (2 min warm-up, 10 min steady state), then both are stopped. Processes are stopped by
# their own PIDs only. The OIDC issuer below is never contacted: nobody logs in, the sessions are minted by
# deploy/load/sessions.mjs. No secret is involved: the database runs with trust authentication on loopback only.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
export PATH=/opt/nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:$PATH
: "${PG_PORT:?}" "${API_PORT:?}" "${RUN_DIR:?}"
REPS="${REPS:-3}" WARMUP_S="${WARMUP_S:-120}" STEADY_S="${STEADY_S:-600}"
WORK="$TMPDIR/load"
mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR" "$WORK/evidence" "$WORK/exports"
url() { echo "postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT/mth?options=-c%20role%3D$1"; }
export MTH_LOAD_DB_URL="postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:$PG_PORT/mth"
export NODE_ENV=production MTH_ENV=load AUTH_MODE=oidc LOG_LEVEL=warn
export APP_BASE_URL="http://localhost:$API_PORT" PORT="$API_PORT"
export OIDC_ISSUER_URL="https://idp.example.invalid/realms/mth-load" OIDC_CLIENT_ID=mth-load OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=not-used-load-run
export DATABASE_URL="$(url mth_app)" DATABASE_OWNER_URL="$(url mth_owner)"
export EVIDENCE_STORAGE_DRIVER=filesystem EVIDENCE_STORAGE_PATH="$WORK/evidence"
unset RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE SEARCH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE EXPORT_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE

API_PID="" WORKER_PID=""
stop() {
  for p in $API_PID $WORKER_PID; do kill -TERM "$p" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  for p in $API_PID $WORKER_PID; do for _ in $(seq 1 100); do kill -0 "$p" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done; done
  for p in $API_PID $WORKER_PID; do kill -KILL "$p" 2>/dev/null || true; done
  API_PID="" WORKER_PID=""
}
trap stop EXIT
start() {
  node apps/worker/dist/main.js >>"$WORK/worker-$1.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
  WORKER_PID=$!
  node apps/api/dist/main.js >>"$WORK/api-$1.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
  API_PID=$!
  for _ in $(seq 1 120); do curl -fsS "http://localhost:$API_PORT/readyz" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0; sleep 0.5; done
  echo "API not ready"; tail -50 "$WORK/api-$1.log"; return 1
}

echo "== driver start $(date -u +%FT%TZ); git HEAD $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
sha256sum deploy/load/generate.mjs deploy/load/sessions.mjs deploy/load/workload.mjs deploy/load/report.mjs

echo "== sessions $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
node deploy/load/sessions.mjs --duration-minutes 240 --out "$WORK/sessions.json"

echo "== search index: start the worker so it runs the requested search.reindex $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
start index
for _ in $(seq 1 360); do
  n=$(psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select count(*) from search_index_state where status = 'idle' and documents_count is not null")
  t=$(psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select count(*) from search_index_state")
  [ "$t" -gt 0 ] && [ "$n" = "$t" ] && break
  sleep 5
done
psql "$MTH_LOAD_DB_URL" -qAtc "select record_type, status, documents_count, last_audit_seq from search_index_state order by 1"
echo "search index ready: $n of $t types $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
stop

echo "== infrastructure $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
node deploy/load/report.mjs capture-infra --out "$RUN_DIR/infrastructure.json" --pgdata "$WORK/pgroot/pg" \
  --api-processes 1 --api-pool 20 --worker-processes 1 --worker-pool 5

for rep in $(seq 1 "$REPS"); do
  echo "== repetition $rep: fresh API and worker $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  start "rep$rep"
  set +e
  node deploy/load/workload.mjs --sessions "$WORK/sessions.json" --base-url "http://127.0.0.1:$API_PORT" \
    --out "$RUN_DIR/rep-$rep" --warmup-s "$WARMUP_S" --steady-s "$STEADY_S" --repetition "$rep"
  rc=$?
  set -e
  echo "repetition $rep workload exit=$rc $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  stop
  grep -c '"level":50' "$WORK/api-rep$rep.log" | sed 's/^/api error-level log lines: /' || true
  [ "$rc" = 0 ] || exit "$rc"
done

echo "== report $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
node deploy/load/report.mjs report --run "$RUN_DIR" --title "DG6 load run 1 (first run, draft report; T-DG6-DO-F)"
echo "== driver end $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
